title: Differentiate nonuniform three-point samples
prompt: Implement solve(payload) for x_m and y, each with exactly three samples. x_m is measured in metres and must be strictly increasing. Fit the unique quadratic through all three points and return its first and second derivatives at the middle coordinate: {"first_per_m":...,"second_per_m2":...}. y has dimensionless units. Let h0=x1-x0, h1=x2-x1, s0=(y1-y0)/h0 and s1=(y2-y1)/h1; the first derivative is (h1*s0+h0*s1)/(h0+h1), and the second is 2*(s1-s0)/(h0+h1). Do not assume uniform spacing. Nonincreasing x returns {"error":"x_order"}. Exactly three valid finite samples are always supplied. Any numeric inputs are finite; inputs have the documented shapes; unspecified validation is out of scope. Do not mutate payload or any nested value. Numeric absolute tolerance 1e-9, relative tolerance 1e-9; strings, booleans, errors and collection shapes must match exactly.
